maintainer_note: Curated reference for optional tools and research candidates. Checked dates record source review; supported package ranges record repository compatibility. Evaluate candidates on synthetic fixtures before adding dependencies.

refresh_before: claiming a package is current, active, deprecated, or archived
turning a watchlist or sidecar tool into an adapter

decision_rules.description: Core engine remains stdlib-first; heavy scientific tools are optional adapters or sidecars.
Use BoFire only for non-box constraints, multi-objective optimization, multi-fidelity scale structure, or explicit operator request.
GPL and AGPL tools are boundary-only or avoid unless repository distribution posture is explicitly changed.
Do not add workflow platforms that duplicate the campaign manifest and task-request contracts unless repeated computational DAGs justify another workflow language.

tools.name: BoFire
tools.posture: primary optional adaptive adapter
tools.current_signal: PyPI 0.5.0 is current upstream. The primary adapter remains on bofire>=0.3.1,<0.4 because later releases require Python 3.11 or newer and carry breaking API and dependency changes. BoFire 0.4 tagged generalized NChooseK DoE support; the separate adaptive-nchoosek-doe extra pins 0.4.1 as an unverified candidate. Upstream 0.5.0 also describes an LLMStrategy; its API and failure behavior have not been tested with this adapter.
tools.fit: Constrained media optimization, mixed spaces, multi-objective BO, and future scale-fidelity planning.
tools.risks: Heavy Torch/BoTorch stack; pre-1.0 API; fermentation phase and feed semantics remain BioSymphony-owned. The 0.3.1 audit found failures for SoboStrategy with NChooseK and multi-fidelity strategies with non-box constraints. The related upstream issues are closed, but later tags have not been retested here; retain OMLT, ENTMOOT, and parallel-arm fallbacks.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Write bofire_strategy_report.json and fall back to stdlib planning when missing or untranslated.

tools.name: pydoe
tools.posture: current lightweight DOE-family backend to evaluate against the shipped pyDOE3 adapter
tools.current_signal: PyPI 1.5.0 is current upstream. This repository still ships its classical-design compatibility adapter through the pydoe3 extra.
tools.fit: Plackett-Burman, factorial, RSM, and Latin-hypercube style fast paths.
tools.risks: No bioprocess constraints, adaptive posterior, or scale-bridge semantics.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Report dependency missing and use stdlib design family where available.

tools.name: pyDOE3
tools.posture: compatibility adapter for extended Box-Behnken and maximin LHS paths
tools.current_signal: PyPI 1.6.2 is current upstream. The compatibility-only status describes this repository's existing adapter route, not the upstream project's maintenance status.
tools.fit: Existing pyDOE3-specific adapter for larger Box-Behnken coverage and maximin Latin-hypercube generation.
tools.risks: The adapter covers a narrow subset of pyDOE3. Evaluate current pydoe before adding new classical-design dependency surface.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Report pyDOE3 missing and use pydoe or stdlib design family where available.

tools.name: SciPy
tools.posture: optional statistical and quasi-random design adapter
tools.current_signal: PyPI 1.18.1 is current upstream and requires Python 3.12 or newer. The repository retains scipy>=1.11 for its wider Python support and uses scipy.stats and scipy.stats.qmc through optional paths.
tools.fit: Small-sample p-values, power quantiles, and quasi-random space-filling designs.
tools.risks: SciPy improves statistical calculations and design generation but does not validate assay quality or campaign conclusions.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Use stdlib distribution approximations and space-filling generators when SciPy is absent.

tools.name: SALib
tools.posture: optional diagnostics adapter
tools.current_signal: PyPI 1.5.2 remains current upstream.
tools.fit: PAWN, delta, and Sobol sensitivity analysis for factor prioritization and assumption checks.
tools.risks: Not an optimizer; precision depends on declared ranges and response models.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Skip optional sensitivity outputs and preserve the base dossier.

tools.name: Frictionless Framework
tools.posture: CSV/table schema reference; stdlib validator remains default
tools.current_signal: PyPI 5.19.0 is current upstream. The stdlib validator remains the default runtime path.
tools.fit: CSV/table contracts for ledgers, evidence tables, result templates, inventories, and run sheets.
tools.risks: Table-shape validation is not scientific semantics.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Stdlib table_contracts validator remains authoritative when the package is absent.

tools.name: Plotly.py
tools.posture: optional interactive charts for the BoFire HTML report
tools.current_signal: PyPI 7.0.0 is current upstream. The public reporter uses Plotly for feasibility slices, candidate cost stacks, and factor-coverage heatmaps.
tools.fit: Interactive charts in standalone BoFire HTML reports.
tools.risks: Embedded JavaScript increases report size; the tabular report remains authoritative.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Omit Plotly sections and preserve the stdlib tabular report when Plotly is absent.

tools.name: RO-Crate
tools.posture: minimal dossier provenance envelope
tools.license: Apache-2.0 docs/spec materials; verify implementation package if added
tools.current_signal: RO-Crate 1.3.0 and rocrate 0.15.1 are current upstream references. Keep the repository's stdlib metadata writer authoritative unless a profile-aware validator is adopted and tested.
tools.fit: Dossier metadata, file inventory, hashes, source refs, license, claim boundaries, and future workflow-run provenance.
tools.risks: JSON-LD can become overbuilt; validator and package APIs add churn. Keep a minimal crate profile and treat profile-aware validation as optional.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Dossier check fails if required ro-crate-metadata.json is missing.

tools.name: ELN file format (.eln)
tools.posture: ELN/LIMS-neutral run-packet interchange candidate built on RO-Crate conventions
tools.current_signal: The consortium specifies a ZIP archive built on RO-Crate and lists implementations with import/export support. Compatibility varies by implementation; a round-trip test remains necessary.
tools.fit: Public-safe synthetic run packets, sample tables, and dossier exports that should move across ELN/LIMS tools without encoding private tracker details.
tools.risks: Import behavior varies across ELNs and the format still carries implementation quirks; do not claim validated ELN compatibility without round-trip fixture tests.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Keep the existing run packet and table contracts authoritative when .eln export is absent or not round-trip tested.

tools.name: GROBID
tools.posture: public scholarly PDF structuring sidecar for open-access evidence
tools.current_signal: GROBID 0.9.1 is the current tagged release.
tools.fit: Convert public or open-license PDFs into structured TEI/BibTeX/citation-context inputs for dossier evidence tables.
tools.risks: Java/Docker service surface; copyright boundaries are source-specific. Do not ingest paywalled or non-permitted full text into public fixtures.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Use PubMed fixture mode or manually curated evidence rows when GROBID is unavailable or source license is unclear.

tools.name: OpenAlex official CLI/API
tools.posture: broad public literature and citation-graph context source
tools.license: MIT for client tooling; OpenAlex data is CC0
tools.current_signal: Official authentication documentation permits basic keyless queries and raises the daily allowance with an API key. Verify endpoint budgets before a harvest; article reuse rights remain separate from metadata access.
tools.fit: Citation graph, topic, institution, and source metadata context beyond PubMed when building public literature dossiers.
tools.risks: API keys and billing/rate limits must stay outside repos and fixtures; metadata breadth does not imply source quality or full-text rights.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Skip OpenAlex enrichment and preserve fixture-backed PubMed/manual evidence rows when the API is unavailable.

tools.name: Europe PMC APIs
tools.posture: public life-science literature and annotations source
tools.license: API/source records vary by article and endpoint
tools.current_signal: The official REST service documents literature search, references, citations, status updates, and open-access full-text XML; the annotations API supplies text-mined terms. Endpoint documentation was reviewed; live ingestion was not tested.
tools.fit: Complement PubMed MCP for public literature harvesting, preprint coverage, open full-text lookup, and concept evidence tables.
tools.risks: Full-text reuse depends on article license; API responses must be fixture-backed in tests and source licenses must be recorded in dossiers.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Skip Europe PMC enrichment and keep existing citation fixtures when the endpoint is unavailable or source rights are unclear.

tools.name: Nox
tools.posture: repo task lane runner
tools.current_signal: PyPI 2026.8.17 is current upstream. The repository retains nox>=2024.4 as its supported development-tool floor.
tools.fit: Stable command surface for unit, table_contracts, dossier_smoke, adaptive_smoke, adaptive_live, and release checks.
tools.risks: Not an environment lock by itself.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Direct Python scripts remain callable without Nox.

tools.name: BoTorch
tools.posture: low-level expert backend
tools.current_signal: PyPI 0.18.1 is current upstream and requires Python 3.11 or newer. The repository keeps a broad lower bound for its narrow optional adapter and does not claim untested latest-version compatibility.
tools.fit: Custom acquisition experiments when BoFire abstractions block a needed route.
tools.risks: Too low-level for campaign-facing contracts and easy to overfit into research code.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Prefer BoFire; if direct BoTorch route fails, write route report and fall back.

tools.name: Xopt
tools.posture: arbitrary scientific optimization and experiment-control comparison backend
tools.current_signal: PyPI lists 3.2.2, released 2026-09-03, requiring Python >=3.11. This source check does not establish adapter compatibility.
tools.fit: Candidate comparison backend for constrained media fixtures, scale-bridge simulations, and arbitrary expensive objective loops when manifest boundaries are preserved.
tools.risks: Accelerator/control-systems origin; BioSymphony must own assay readiness, constraint translation, cost/scale semantics, and candidate-table validation.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not emit Xopt candidates as authoritative designs until a fixture route report exists; fall back to BoFire, ENTMOOT, OMLT, BoTorch, or stdlib planning.

tools.name: Trieste
tools.posture: TensorFlow-based BO research toolbox and complex-acquisition comparison target
tools.current_signal: PyPI 4.6.0 remains current upstream. Public docs describe ask-tell, batch, asynchronous, constrained, multi-fidelity, and multi-objective BO.
tools.fit: Useful landscape comparison for complex follow-up planning and acquisition-function research, especially when TensorFlow/GPflow is already present in an external evaluation lane.
tools.risks: Heavy TensorFlow/GPflow stack and no fermentation-specific semantics; not a near-term public adapter unless a fixture demonstrates a route that BoFire/BayBE/Ax do not cover.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not add as dependency or campaign route without an explicit evaluation report.

tools.name: pymoo
tools.posture: candidate-table Pareto and tournament sidecar
tools.current_signal: PyPI 0.6.2 is current upstream and provides constrained and mixed-variable multi-objective algorithms.
tools.fit: Posthoc Pareto sorting, hypervolume diagnostics, and design-tournament scoring.
tools.risks: Evolutionary optimizer rather than Bayesian sample-efficient planning; use for diagnostics, not as the primary refinement loop.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Keep existing stdlib tournament and emit no pymoo report when unavailable.

tools.name: SMT
tools.posture: scale-bridge surrogate diagnostic candidate
tools.current_signal: PyPI lists SMT 2.15.0, released 2026-09-08. The related SMT-optim 0.1.3 package offers constrained mixed-variable and multi-fidelity comparison methods; these routes remain untested here.
tools.fit: Co-kriging and multi-fidelity surrogate diagnostics for plate/flask/reactor bridges.
tools.risks: Surrogate toolbox, not campaign optimizer; requires careful adapter design.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Keep scale_recipe and BoFire route reports; do not block dossier compilation.

tools.name: Pyomo.DAE
tools.posture: advanced feed/profile feasibility sidecar
tools.current_signal: Pyomo 6.10.1 is current upstream. Pyomo.DAE remains a candidate sidecar for dynamic fed-batch and feed-control feasibility models.
tools.fit: Continuous feed profile optimization, volume/substrate/oxygen constraints, and dynamic feasibility.
tools.risks: Solver stack and initialization can become site-specific and heavy.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not run dynamic optimization; preserve static feasibility warnings.

tools.name: PyPlate
tools.posture: plate/deep-well recipe sidecar candidate
tools.current_signal: PyPI 0.4.7 remains the latest release; the upstream repository has newer activity. Keep as an evaluation candidate for high-throughput experiment representation.
tools.fit: Plate recipe exports, well-volume checks, reagent transforms, and liquid-handling artifacts.
tools.risks: Plate-centric; not a fermentation scale-bridge model.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Emit BioSymphony plate manifest only; do not claim liquid-handler readiness.

tools.name: FedBatchDesigner
tools.posture: reference model/example candidate
tools.current_signal: The 2025-07-11 publication snapshot remains the latest tagged release. It provides constant and exponential feeding models, case-study notebooks, and CSV or image export.
tools.fit: Feed-volume/time stage math and growth-arrested fed-batch planning references.
tools.risks: Low adoption signal; may not cover ordinary microbial or mammalian fed-batch oxygen limits.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Keep BioSymphony feed policy fields and skip reference comparison.

tools.name: BioSTEAM
tools.posture: cost/downstream sidecar
tools.license: University of Illinois/NCSA Open Source License
tools.current_signal: PyPI 2.53.11 is current and the upstream repository remains active. BioSTEAM stays an evaluation candidate for process-economic and life-cycle sidecars, not a core DoE planner.
tools.fit: Cost/L, downstream context, feedstock/media cost projections, TEA/LCA examples.
tools.risks: Biorefinery scope can distract from upstream executability.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Use existing cost_rollup with declared assumptions.

tools.name: SBML runtime stack (libRoadRunner/Tellurium/AMICI)
tools.posture: model import/export sidecar
tools.current_signal: Current tagged components are libRoadRunner 2.10.0, Tellurium 2.2.11.2, and AMICI 1.0.1. Keep this stack as a mechanistic-model and parameter-estimation sidecar candidate.
tools.fit: Growth/substrate/product kinetics, parameter tables, event/feed schedules, and model provenance.
tools.risks: Public SBML models rarely encode full vessel/feed/oxygen-transfer semantics.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Record model as external evidence and skip runtime execution.

tools.name: PEtab / libpetab-python
tools.posture: parameter-estimation table contract candidate for mechanistic sidecars
tools.current_signal: PyPI lists 0.9.0, released 2026-09-07, requiring Python >=3.12. This source check does not establish adapter compatibility.
tools.fit: Portable public calibration fixtures around SBML/ODE models before pyPESTO, AMICI, or RoadRunner-side evaluation.
tools.risks: Systems-biology parameter-estimation semantics are not fermentation manifest semantics; keep response, factor, assay, cost, and scale contracts BioSymphony-owned.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Skip PEtab export/import and keep the campaign manifest plus table contracts authoritative when no validated PEtab fixture exists.

tools.name: pyPESTO
tools.posture: parameter-estimation and uncertainty sidecar for public mechanistic models
tools.current_signal: PyPI lists 0.7.0, released 2026-09-09, requiring Python >=3.11. This source check does not establish adapter compatibility.
tools.fit: Candidate calibration sidecar for public or synthetic kinetic and cell-culture models, with uncertainty reports that can feed evidence and assumption checks.
tools.risks: Heavy optional stack and calibration outputs can look more authoritative than the available data supports; never bypass readiness, assay-power, scale, or claim-boundary checks.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Treat pyPESTO results as external evidence rows unless an in-repo fixture validates the full route; skip calibration when dependencies or model contracts are absent.

tools.name: Pseudobatch
tools.posture: fed-batch sample-withdrawal correction reference and preprocessing candidate
tools.current_signal: The repository provides concentration-data transformations and separate uncertainty propagation through CmdStan. Source inspection supports a preprocessing evaluation; no integration or release upgrade was tested.
tools.fit: Preprocessing note for public fed-batch ledgers before growth-rate, biomass, or response modeling when sample withdrawal creates mass-balance artifacts.
tools.risks: Specific correction method, not a general fermentation simulator or scale-transfer model; error-propagation extra brings CmdStan complexity.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Leave raw and corrected values explicit in evidence tables; skip transformation when volume/sample metadata are missing.

tools.name: Pixi
tools.posture: future multi-environment lock/task candidate
tools.current_signal: Pixi 0.78.0 is current upstream. It remains a watch item for reproducible optional dependency lanes if the current venv and Nox approach becomes insufficient.
tools.fit: Named environments for stdlib, contracts, adaptive, release, and optional-tool smoke profiles.
tools.risks: Adds another environment manager.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Continue using direct Python scripts and Nox.

tools.name: Common Workflow Language / cwltool provenance
tools.posture: portable workflow handoff candidate
tools.current_signal: CWL and CWLProv remain active; cwltool 3.2.20260720092025 is current. Keep as a watch item for portable declared inputs, outputs, and workflow provenance.
tools.fit: Narrow remote execution bundles with explicit command provenance.
tools.risks: Verbose for simple scripts and unnecessary while the manifest and task-request contracts remain sufficient.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Use Nox plus the explicit JSON handoff contracts.

tools.name: DWSIM
tools.posture: external export/import only
tools.current_signal: DWSIM 9.0.5 is the latest tagged release. The linked GitHub repository is archived; GPL licensing and the heavy runtime keep it boundary-only.
tools.fit: Downstream, biorefinery, and process-economics reference simulations.
tools.risks: GPL embedding risk and GUI/heavy runtime.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not import as dependency; export assumptions only.

tools.name: CADET
tools.posture: external downstream sidecar only
tools.current_signal: CADET-Core 5.1.1 is current upstream. CADET remains relevant to downstream unit-operation modeling and outside the core upstream DoE planner.
tools.fit: Chromatography/filtration sidecars when dossiers grow downstream.
tools.risks: GPL embedding risk and uncertain upstream fermentation fit.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Keep downstream assumptions as evidence rows.

tools.name: COBRApy
tools.posture: evidence sidecar only
tools.current_signal: COBRApy 0.32.1 is current upstream. Keep it boundary-only unless public metabolic-model priors enter the evidence layer.
tools.fit: Substrate/product feasibility priors and yield-bound sanity checks.
tools.risks: GEM predictions are not process readiness; GPL and model-license variance.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Represent model conclusions as reviewed evidence rows only.

tools.name: Snakemake
tools.posture: defer unless repeated computational DAGs dominate
tools.current_signal: Snakemake 9.26.1 is current upstream. It remains a capable workflow engine that is not needed for the repository's current contract and dossier flow.
tools.fit: Benchmark sweeps or repeated simulation campaigns.
tools.risks: Another DSL and execution model competing with existing orchestration.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Keep the manifest, task-request, and Nox lanes.

tools.name: Nextflow
tools.posture: defer unless large cloud/HPC workflows appear
tools.current_signal: Nextflow 26.04.6 is the latest tagged release. Keep it as a watch item for larger containerized pipelines rather than adding a second workflow language now.
tools.fit: Large computational analysis pipelines.
tools.risks: Groovy DSL and cloud-pipeline posture do not align with current Python/stdlib repo shape.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Keep the manifest, task-request, and Nox lanes.

tools.name: scikit-optimize
tools.posture: do not add
tools.current_signal: PyPI 0.10.2 remains the latest release and the original repository remains archived. Use the separately tracked ProcessOptimizer continuation for any new evaluation.
tools.fit: None for new integration.
tools.risks: Stale dependency and limited fit for constrained multi-objective scale-bridge work.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not integrate; keep any legacy references as historical only.

tools.name: pysamoo
tools.posture: do not add without explicit license decision
tools.current_signal: PyPI 0.1.2 remains current while the repository has newer activity. The AGPL license keeps this surrogate-assisted multi-objective tool outside the adopted adapter set.
tools.fit: None for current repo.
tools.risks: AGPL distribution obligations.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not integrate.

tools.name: ENTMOOT v2
tools.posture: in-repo adapter wraps ENTMOOT v2; min_count, min-active coupling, tie-cycle handling, and HiGHS fallback are adapter-enforced
tools.current_signal: PyPI 2.1.1 remains current upstream. The public adapter adds min_count emission, min-active lower coupling, HiGHS solver support, and tie-cycle handling at the repository boundary.
tools.fit: MIP-encoded NChooseK cardinality first-class; addresses BoFire NChooseK+SoboStrategy stall (issue #450). In-repo adapter exposes adapter_backed_nchoosek BO route with HiGHS default solver.
tools.risks: Raw upstream ENTMOOT APIs can still mislead if used directly; use the in-repo adapter so min_count, min-active coupling, solver fallback, and fail-closed route reports are preserved.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Adapter raises RuntimeError at instantiation if entmoot or chosen solver not available; degrades to "not_available" in plan reports without raising.

tools.name: PubMed MCP Adapter
tools.posture: in-repo adapter normalises PubMed records into the CITATIONS.json schema. Fixture mode is the primary integration path; the direct MCP hook (_try_mcp_fetch) is a stub awaiting an in-process bridge. Live enrichment is harness-mediated and fed in via fixtures.
tools.current_signal: The in-repo adapter supports fixture normalization and fallback behavior. Direct in-process MCP calls remain unwired; live retrieval must be performed by the calling harness and handed to the fixture interface.
tools.fit: Fixture-driven PubMed citation enrichment, dossier BibTeX export, --use-pubmed-fixture CLI flag for deterministic test mode. A direct in-process MCP hook is reserved (_try_mcp_fetch).
tools.risks: Direct MCP mode is currently a stub; the practical path for live enrichment is harness-mediated harvest plus fixture handoff. Fixture mode required for offline/CI runs.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: When MCP unreachable, adapter falls back to fixture mode or empty enrichment with explicit warning.

tools.name: Ax
tools.posture: adaptive experimentation infrastructure and custom-generation-strategy candidate; not default static DoE route
tools.current_signal: PyPI 1.3.1 is current upstream and requires Python 3.11 or newer. The backend-eval extra remains pinned to 1.2.4, so this entry does not claim latest-version compatibility.
tools.fit: Production adaptive-experiment orchestration, custom GenerationStrategy/BoTorch routing, trial lifecycle and resume semantics when a campaign outgrows a simple ask/tell adapter.
tools.risks: Heavier translation surface than BoFire or BayBE; not chemistry-first or bioprocess-first; can duplicate campaign orchestration if adopted too early.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not block dossier compilation; if Ax is unavailable or cannot preserve the manifest boundary, write an evaluation report and fall back to BoFire, direct BoTorch, or stdlib planning.

tools.name: BoTorch (direct usage, EIpu)
tools.posture: alternative cost-aware BO path bypassing BoFire abstraction
tools.current_signal: PyPI 0.18.1 is current upstream. A dated repository review selected direct BoTorch as the watch path for cost-aware acquisition experiments that need lower-level surrogate control.
tools.fit: Expected Improvement per unit cost (EIpu) for cost-aware Pareto front; direct surrogate control without BoFire constraint-translation overhead.
tools.risks: Reimplements problem encoding from scratch; loses BoFire's data-model + factor-space scaffolding.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: N/A — not wired.

tools.name: Atlas (gryffin/golem successor)
tools.posture: tree-based BO with categorical-aware kernels
tools.current_signal: The canonical repository is now under the-matter-lab. The last reviewed release was v0.0.1; this remains a watch item for categorical and unknown-feasibility workflows.
tools.fit: Unknown-feasibility BO via Anubis variational GP classifier. Multi-fidelity also supported. NOT a NChooseK fix — use ENTMOOT (via BoFire EntingStrategy) for cardinality.
tools.risks: Smaller community than BoFire/BoTorch; chemistry-first not bioprocess-first.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: N/A — not wired.

tools.name: BayBe (Bayesian Back End)
tools.posture: low-data/hybrid/transfer-learning BO comparison target next to BoFire; Apache-2.0
tools.current_signal: PyPI 0.15.0 is current upstream and supports Python >=3.10,<3.15. The backend-eval extra remains pinned to 0.14.3 because 0.15.0 includes breaking API changes; no latest-version compatibility is claimed.
tools.fit: Compare next to BoFire for low-data-regime design, discrete/hybrid campaign surfaces, transfer-learning across related campaigns, asynchronous result arrival, and substance/categorical encodings. Good match to cumulative-dossier learning if kept behind a manifest boundary.
tools.risks: Smaller classical constrained-DoE/IPOPT surface than BoFire and a pre-1.0 API. Any adapter must preserve the manifest, scale-bridge, assay, cost-stack, and handoff boundaries.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not materialize BayBE candidates as authoritative designs until a fixture route report exists. If BayBE is missing or cannot preserve the manifest boundary, write an evaluation report and fall back to BoFire or stdlib planning.

tools.name: obsidian (Algorithmic Process Optimization)
tools.posture: GPL-3.0 boundary-only; documented as Dash UI + SHAP pattern exemplar
tools.current_signal: PyPI 0.8.6 remains the latest release and the repository remains active. The project provides GP-based Bayesian optimization, batch recommendations, and an optional application UI.
tools.fit: Reference for Dash UI patterns and SHAP-based explainability for process development scientists. Not embeddable due to GPL-3.0.
tools.risks: GPL-3.0 embedding risk per registry license_boundary decision rule. Closed-source corporate-affiliated maintainer (Merck & Co.).
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not import as dependency; document patterns only.

tools.name: estim8 (JuBiotech parameter estimation)
tools.posture: AGPL-3.0 boundary-only; FMI bridge for Modelica parameter estimation
tools.current_signal: PyPI 0.1.6 is current upstream. The package supports FMI-based parameter estimation for dynamic bioprocess models.
tools.fit: First-class FMI bridge — can ingest Modelica models from external upstream model authors and run estimation in Python. Useful when a campaign sponsor brings Modelica vessel/control models.
tools.risks: AGPL-3.0 prohibits embedding under the registry license boundary. Maintenance horizon remains uncertain.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not import; treat operator-run results as external evidence rows.

tools.name: bletl (JuBiotech BioLector parser)
tools.posture: AGPL-3.0 boundary-only; BioLector raw-file parser with PyMC inference
tools.current_signal: PyPI 1.7.1 remains current and the repository remains active. The package parses BioLector data and provides uncertainty-aware growth-rate analysis.
tools.fit: Canonical Python ingest path for BioLector microbioreactor data. Operator runs externally; biosymphony ingests CSV output.
tools.risks: AGPL-3.0 prohibits embedding per registry license_boundary decision rule. Previous survey did not flag the AGPL license; this entry exists to make the boundary explicit.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not import; ingest CSV exports as evidence rows.

tools.name: ProcessOptimizer (Novo Nordisk scikit-optimize fork)
tools.posture: scikit-optimize maintained continuation; pharma-affiliated maintainer
tools.current_signal: PyPI 1.1.2 is current upstream. The maintained scikit-optimize lineage provides Gaussian-process, multi-objective, batch, and plotting features.
tools.fit: Migration target when campaign sponsor brings scikit-optimize code. Lighter than BoFire/BayBe; keeps the scikit-optimize lineage alive.
tools.risks: Smaller ecosystem signal than BoFire/BayBe. Inherits scikit-optimize's pre-existing limitations (no NChooseK first-class, no cost-aware).
tools.fail_closed_behavior: N/A — not wired.

tools.name: TabPFN (foundation-model surrogate)
tools.posture: optional low-data surrogate adapter; this repository requires a runtime token for noninteractive use
tools.license: Prior Labs License for code and v2 weights; non-commercial license for default TabPFN-3 weights
tools.current_signal: PyPI lists 9.0.0, released 2026-09-15, requiring Python >=3.10. This source check does not establish adapter compatibility. The supported extra remains tabpfn>=8,<9; version 9 requires a separate compatibility and checkpoint-license review.
tools.fit: Low-data tabular regression surrogate for sequential planning when n<20 or the operator explicitly requests a TabPFN-backed planning experiment.
tools.risks: Default TabPFN-3 weights are non-commercial, while the code and v2 weights carry the Prior Labs License with an attribution provision. Review terms before use. No native NChooseK ownership; the repository wrapper and post-hoc validation handle constraints. Predictions are model suggestions, not lab validation.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Adapter remains importable without token or package; plan reports degrade to not_available and stdlib fallback remains authoritative.

tools.name: TabICLv2
tools.posture: open tabular foundation-model watch item next to TabPFN
tools.current_signal: PyPI 2.2.0 was released 2026-09-02. The upstream change log documents quantile regression support; interval coverage and acquisition behavior remain untested here.
tools.fit: Watch as a possible TabPFN comparison surrogate for larger public result tables, especially when zero-tuning tabular regression is useful but TabPFN's small-data posture is limiting.
tools.risks: No native DoE constraint ownership, assay semantics, or scale context; checkpoint download and GPU memory behavior need a fixture before any adapter work.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Do not add as dependency or route until a fixture shows constraint-preserving regression behavior under BioSymphony validation.

tools.name: LLAMBO (LLM-warmstart sampler)
tools.posture: LLM warmstart pilot candidate via OptunaHub; warmstart-only scope
tools.current_signal: The 2025 reproducibility preprint reports contextual warmstart gains on Bayesmark and HPOBench. These benchmark findings do not establish fermentation performance or a general trial-count advantage.
tools.fit: Evaluate contextual warmstarts against random and space-filling initialization on held-out synthetic objectives. Performance depends on task, prompt, and model; no general improvement is established here.
tools.risks: Results depend on prompts, model, and benchmark. The OptunaHub sampler uses random sampling for categorical variables. External inference requires explicit service configuration and cost approval.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Keep standard initialization unless a reproducible fixture supports the proposed warmstart.

tools.name: OMLT (Optimization & Machine Learning Toolkit)
tools.posture: optional in-repo adapter for MIP-optimized surrogate planning with explicit linear and NChooseK constraints
tools.current_signal: PyPI 1.2.2 remains current upstream. The public optional adapter is import-safe without heavy dependencies and emits not_available or solver_unavailable reports unless its solver and surrogate stack is installed.
tools.fit: MIP-backed surrogate optimization for linear, categorical, and NChooseK-heavy candidate generation when a fitted surrogate plus hard constraints is the right planning surface.
tools.risks: Surrogate quality bounds candidate quality; solver stack is heavier than stdlib/BoFire. It must not bypass BioSymphony readiness, assay, evidence, cost, or scale-transfer gates.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Adapter remains importable without optional dependencies; plan reports degrade to not_available or solver_unavailable without raising.

tools.name: Docling
tools.posture: local document-table extraction candidate
tools.license: MIT code; check each model license
tools.current_signal: The 2025 technical report and current repository describe layout-aware parsing and structured document exports. Source reviewed; extraction quality is untested here.
tools.fit: Extract table cells and page coordinates from public PDFs or office files before citation normalization.
tools.risks: Model downloads add size; OCR can corrupt units, symbols, or footnotes. Bibliographic identity still needs a separate check.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Keep source-linked manual evidence rows when extraction or page attribution fails.

tools.name: olmOCR 2
tools.posture: vision OCR fallback candidate
tools.license: Apache-2.0 code and olmOCR-2-7B-1025 weights; input rights vary
tools.current_signal: The October 2025 paper describes a vision-based document conversion model. The repository provides local GPU and remote-server routes; neither is tested here.
tools.fit: Compare extraction on scanned or image-heavy pages that defeat the primary parser.
tools.risks: A 7B model adds substantial compute and storage. Remote mode transmits documents; source rights and service terms require review.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Retain the source page for manual review; never infer a missing numeric value.

tools.name: PaperQA2
tools.posture: citation-backed literature synthesis candidate
tools.license: Apache-2.0 code; model and article terms vary
tools.current_signal: The repository documents agentic retrieval over local documents and citation-bearing answers. Local model configurations exist; defaults can use hosted services.
tools.fit: Draft evidence summaries with source spans for reviewer approval.
tools.risks: A citation can be real but fail to support the claim. Hosted inference can incur costs and transfer source text.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Preserve manual citation rows unless passage support and service authorization are confirmed.

tools.name: TabTune
tools.posture: optional calibration benchmark candidate
tools.license: MIT code; each model retains its checkpoint terms
tools.current_signal: The November 2025 preprint introduces a shared tabular-model interface. Current source documents conformal prediction, recalibration, and grouped or temporal evaluation.
tools.fit: Compare TabPFN and TabICL uncertainty on the same synthetic data splits before using predictions in acquisition.
tools.risks: Model dependencies and checkpoints add weight. Conformal coverage relies on exchangeability; sequential design and shifted data need separate diagnostics.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Retain existing surrogate reports when model terms, dependencies, or held-out coverage checks are unresolved.

tools.name: GOLLuM
tools.posture: language-informed GP research candidate
tools.license: Apache-2.0 code; model and benchmark terms require separate review
tools.current_signal: The August 28, 2026 article studies language representations trained through GP marginal likelihood across 23 optimization tasks. Public research code is available; no package release or local benchmark was verified.
tools.fit: Compare language-informed representations with GP and TabPFN baselines on a synthetic mixed-factor fixture.
tools.risks: Published tasks emphasize chemistry and materials. Compute requirements, checkpoint terms, and hard-constraint translation need separate evaluation.
tools.fail_closed_behavior: Keep existing GP or stdlib planning unless an isolated fixture preserves constraints and records model provenance.
